acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Celestials family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Warden, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Four-Wing Axis Adjudicator (Specialist) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two fire construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A composed four-winged humanoid in ornate gold armor, with upper and lower feather pairs, two independently rotating halo rings, and sacred script drifting in ordered bands around both arms.

Signature mechanic: Double Injunction: the upper wing pair rotates the outer halo ring and a line of script clockwise; the lower pair rotates the inner ring counterclockwise. Their projected axes sweep the arena, and where matching script meets becomes a damaging lock. Where unlike glyphs cross, both rings stall and reveal the central gold bearing as a safe attack window.
battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the floor into intersecting-axis control by rotating two halo rings with separate wing pairs, creating one forbidden crossing and one deliberately safe quadrant.
constructionDimensions: Ordered regalia becomes a solar kiln beyond native light through heat-crazed gold, ceramic halo vents, char-edged feathers, ember channels inside marble armor, and furnace-like ring bearings scaled from the T1 simple halo to the T5 orrery.

Actions follow counted combustion cycles: vents open in sequence, specific wing pairs fan intake, heat distortion marks a selected decree, and a dark cooling bearing exposes the alignment after release.
counterplay: Track unlike glyphs rather than brightness, move into their crossing, and strike the exposed central bearing while both wing pairs pause; staying between matching glyphs triggers the lock. Affinity signal: The selected halo bearing darkens and its ceramic vent remains open after a solar cycle; striking it breaks that alignment without extinguishing family-native radiance.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only fire treatment or extra gold-orange applied to family-native sunlight colors
Glow-only fire treatment without kiln materials, intake behavior, and a cooling bearing
Generic fire wings that erase feather count, wing roots, and ordered motion
Brighter family-native light presented as Fire affinity without combustion construction
identityInvariants: An idealized upright humanoid silhouette remains deliberately symmetrical, with feathered wings and a halo above or behind the head even as the body becomes increasingly abstract.
White, ivory, pale gold, sunlight yellow, and sky blue remain family-native ordered radiance rather than elemental affinity colors.
Polished gold, white marble, feather, silk, and source-native pure light stay layered so armor, cloth, wing roots, halo joints, and the suggested body remain readable.
Halos, ring geometry, sacred script, ribbons, censers, blank ceremonial masks, and wing count communicate rank through exact symmetry and moving parts rather than glow or size alone.
Escalation increases wing pairs and halo complexity from a simple ring to an orrery, but each tier preserves a breakable alignment joint and a learnable ordered command.
telegraph: Four wings separate into upper and lower pairs, two halo rings turn in opposite directions, and script drifts from the arms to mark both projected axes before they move.
